In Proceedings of the ACM/IEEE 29th International Conference on Model Driven Engineering Languages and Systems (MODELS '26), Málaga, Spain, pp. 470-475. ACM. doi:10.1145/3822455.3838778. Full text read from arXiv:2511.02475v3 [cs.SE], 27 Aug 2026
Conference — MODELS '26 (ACM/IEEE 29th International Conference on Model Driven Engineering Languages and Systems), 6 pages; read from the arXiv v3 version
TU Wien, Austria: Software Engineering Group (Cito), Business Informatics Group (Bork)

Conceptual; secondary: Proposes an approach — position/vision paper arguing for a renewed role of software models recovered from AI-generated systems; proposes model-mediated feedback loops (agentic and human reflective), illustrated by a public anecdote and a hardening scenario; no evaluation
fields.why: Main vs secondary is a judgement: the paper proposes model-mediated feedback loops ('We propose', p. 3) with model types (Table 1) and a scenario, which could make Proposes an approach the main nature; it also describes itself as a conceptual reframing needing empirical evaluation (p. 5), which supports Conceptual

fields.v: Model-mediated feedback loops for AI-generated software (no name or version): software models recovered post hoc from generated code, used in an agentic loop (automated checking and repair) and a human reflective loop (inspection and revision of assumptions)

Recovered software models (Table 1): domain and data model, behavioural model, architectural model, constraint model, runtime model; linked to code, tests, traces and prompts with evidence and confidence markers; derived regression tests, static checks, repair prompts, model edits

Human intent/prompts -> agent generates system -> recover models from code -> symbolic checks (model checking, analysis, tests, policy checks) -> refinement (repair prompts, model edits) -> recovery and checking repeat; human reflective loop in parallel. Runs at natural pauses: before deployment, after agentic change, on test failure, when a prototype gains users, during review
Human inspects recovered models in the reflective loop; inferred constraints must be validated by the creator or an authoritative policy before enforcement
